faqs.a: A ZIP archive is a single file that holds many files inside it. Recipients download once and unzip to get every PDF back with its original name.
The tool uses the stored (uncompressed) method so it runs instantly on any file. PDF files are already compressed internally, so re-compressing them would barely shrink anything anyway.
faqs.q: Are the PDFs compressed inside the ZIP?

faqs.a: Yes. The archive follows the standard ZIP format with correct CRC32 checksums, so Windows Explorer, macOS Archive Utility, 7-Zip and phone file managers all open it.
faqs.q: Will the ZIP open on my phone?

faqs.a: Just the total memory of your browser tab. Dozens of files and a few hundred megabytes work fine on a desktop; phones handle smaller bundles more comfortably.
faqs.q: How many PDFs can I add?

faqs.a: The bundle is named after the text you type, ending in .zip. If you leave it blank, the default name pdf-bundle.zip is used.
faqs.q: How is the ZIP file named?

faqs.a: The tool writes every byte of the archive locally with its own ZIP builder — no library, no server, no upload.

pdf-to-zip.formula:
zip_size ≈ sum(pdf_sizes) + (76 + name_length) × file_count

Each file adds a ~76-byte local header plus its UTF-8 name. Because PDFs are already compressed, the stored method adds almost no size — bundling 5 PDFs of 8.0 MB total gives a ZIP of about 8.0 MB.
howTo: Click the file picker and select one or more PDFs.
Review the list — remove anything you added by mistake.
Type a name for your ZIP archive (optional).
Click the bundle button to build the ZIP.
Download the single .zip file and share or archive it.
keyFacts: Multiple PDFs are packed into one standard ZIP archive, entirely in your browser.
The archive uses the stored method: files are packed as-is with correct CRC32 integrity checksums.
Duplicate file names are renamed automatically (report (2).pdf) so nothing is overwritten.
UTF-8 file names are supported, so Hindi, Arabic and other scripts survive the round trip.
A live total shows the combined size of everything you have added before you build.

limitations: Files are stored uncompressed — the ZIP will be roughly the same size as the PDFs combined.
Very large bundles (hundreds of megabytes) may strain low-memory phones.
Password-protected PDFs are packed as-is; the ZIP itself is not encrypted.
File names longer than a few hundred characters may be truncated by some unzip tools.
